key_insight: A coupled pore-scale lattice Boltzmann model shows how temperature-driven salinity changes can make freezing reshape sea-ice brine channels non-uniformly.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports pore-scale analysis of coupled heat transfer, solute redistribution, and evolving geometry in phase-changing porous media.
method: Couple liquid solute transport with conjugate heat transfer across solid and liquid phases.
Use a link-based Volume-of-Pixel formulation for direction-dependent interface motion.
Apply a generalized Robin boundary treatment for solute redistribution at moving interfaces.
evidence_signal: Thermal benchmarks validate phase change, literature tests show first- to second-order convergence for the Robin treatment, and diffusive sea-ice simulations recover ideal mushy-layer behaviour under appropriate scale separation.
watch_item: The sea-ice application is purely diffusive; performance with advective brine transport remains unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: A coupled lattice Boltzmann model for pore-scale mushy-layer dynamics with application to sea ice
